title: Short-term fasting and individualized nutrition accompanying adjuvant chemotherapy for colorectal cancer – a randomized controlled 2-arm intervention study
summary:
This study examines whether individually tailored nutritional counselling in the course of adjuvant chemotherapy can help reduce side effects and improve patients' quality-of-life. Two approaches are compared:
1) Individual nutritional counselling following a detailed nutritional analysis
2) The same nutritional counselling combined with short-term fasting (approx. 45-70 hours) around and during chemotherapy

interventions.name: Group A: Nutritional counseling + short-term fasting (approx. 45-70 hours per chemotherapy cycle)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study will include patients with a confirmed diagnosis of stage II colorectal cancer with high-risk factors or stage III colorectal cancer who are receiving adjuvant systemic chemotherapy with FOLFOX or CAPOX for at least 4 cycles.
Exclusion criteria:
- Existing underweight (BMI < 19kg/m2) or current weight loss >5% of body weight in the last month.
- History of eating disorders (anorexia nervosa, bulimia)
- Known addiction / existing alcohol abuse
- Serious mental illness (e.g., severe depression, schizophrenia)
- Other serious internal medical conditions
- Terminal or serious illness with significant impairment of mobility and overall vitality
- Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus
- No email address or internet access (due to electronic CRF)
- Simultaneous participation in another study
- Language communication difficulties, dementia
